repairs.value: If a loving God could make the relational option unmistakably known without compelling acceptance, goods from uncertainty would not justify even one sincere person's deprivation.

A possible extension is that divine disclosure could secure ordinary, settled awareness of God's availability without determining anyone's response. Knowing that another person exists does not itself produce trust, obedience, affection, or relationship; those attitudes remain open to refusal. If freedom protects unforced love, it may support withholding irresistible experiences, yet it does not by itself explain withholding recognizable access to the alleged partner. On this hypothesis, even one sincere nonbeliever matters because perfect love could preserve choice while removing ignorance of the choice's object, making hiddenness an additional cost requiring justification.
